title: How Often to Replan: Reasons, a Cooldown, and Planning From Where the Vehicle Will Be When the Plan Arrives

questions.question: Why replan for reasons and not on a timer alone?
options: A timer plans too often or too late
questions.explanation: A reason is a thing that went wrong. The vehicle that planned for reasons used 5 plans. A short timer plans constantly for nothing, and a long one plans too late for a wall.

questions.question: The vehicle that never replanned:
options: Stood in front of the wall and never arrived
questions.explanation: Its plan was made before the wall was known. With no reason to plan again it stopped at the safety distance and stayed.

questions.question: Planning every 0.2 s used how many plans, against the reasons' 5?
options: 86, and no quicker (21.4 s against 20.9 s)
questions.explanation: 86 plans to arrive in 21.4 s, against 5 plans and 20.9 s. More planning bought nothing.

questions.question: How long did the vehicle stand and wait with the look-ahead of 0.6 m, against 3 m?
questions.explanation: Noticed 0.6 m ahead, there is no path left to drive while the planner runs. Noticed 3 m ahead, the vehicle keeps moving until the new plan comes.

questions.question: Where should a plan that takes a second begin?
options: Where the vehicle was when planning began
At the nearest point of the old path
Where it will be when the plan arrives: 0.06 m off, and it arrived in 20.1 s
questions.explanation: By the time the plan arrives the vehicle has moved on. Planned from the old position it was 1.16 m off its new path at once, and planned 83 times without arriving.

questions.question: Why may a blocked path bypass the cooldown?
options: It is the cheapest reason to check
Waiting costs a stop or a crash
The cooldown only applies to timers
questions.explanation: The cooldown is there to stop needless planning. A wall ahead is not needless, and a second's wait is a second closer to it.
